Subject: Clarify Eval acceptance & A/B escape criteria for NovaCorp promptset

Hi all —

Quick kickoff note on NovaCorp: they want to run the promptset_v2 through our A/B with an eye toward a staged uplift. Before Karthik starts instrumenting the metrics pipelines, we need product clarity on acceptance thresholds and explicit escape triggers so ops and CS have deterministic rollback behavior.

Attachments: promptset_v2.xlsx (prompt bank), ab_bucket_matrix.csv (proposed bucket sizing) — both attached. Also pasted a short acceptance draft into acceptance_criteria.md (attached).

My asks:
- Product: confirm the single primary metric for acceptance (helpfulness, safety, or a composite?) and hard tolerance for any harm signal.
- SRE/Runtime (Karthik): can you outline what latency/95th we should treat as a non-blocking regression versus a blocking one?
- Eval (Marissa): give the minimum evaluation sample size per bucket and whether we need stratified sampling for the hallucination-sensitive prompts.
- Roadmap (Marcus): if acceptance requires additional model tweaks, what is the minimum runway you need for a canary + fix loop?

Goal: lock acceptance and escape today so we can have an A/B schedule by EOD and start traffic next week.

Thanks — Priya
Priya Natarajan
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Clarify Eval acceptance & A/B escape criteria for NovaCorp promptset

Thanks Priya — quick technical inputs from infra/runtime side:

- Latency: our default SLO is p95 <= 180ms (token-streaming path). For this workload I recommend:
  - non-blocking warning: p95 in (180ms, 250ms] -> log + alert to infra but OK to proceed if quality delta meets bar.
  - blocking: p95 > 250ms or error-rate increase > 0.5% absolute -> automatic throttle to canary or pause (we can automate this).
- Throughput/backpressure: if average tokens/sec drops > 20% for the dedicated pool, we should consider shifting NovaCorp to a lower-concurrency path.
- Observability note: we need the eval triggers to emit the prompt ID and cohort tag so we can correlate quality regressions to specific prompts quickly.

I can wire the metrics in 1-2 working days once acceptance metrics and sample sizes are final.

Karthik
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Clarify Eval acceptance & A/B escape criteria for NovaCorp promptset

Folks — here's the eval POV and proposed numbers (see acceptance_criteria.md attached for a longer rationale):

- Primary metric: "helpfulness@promptset" (binary helpful/unhelpful judged by rubric). Secondary: safety_harm_rate (counts of harmful outputs per 1k responses).
- Acceptance thresholds (suggested):
  - Helpfulness uplift >= +3.0% (A over control) with p < 0.05 on bootstrapped samples.
  - Safety_harm_rate must not increase by > 0.2 harms per 1k responses (absolute). If harm delta > 0.2, fail.
- Sample sizing: per bucket (we will use 4 buckets): minimum n=3,000 responses/bucket to detect a 2.5% uplift with ~80% power. For particularly fragile prompts (see sheet column "fragile=true") we should stratify and oversample to n=5,000.
- Canary plan: start with 1% traffic for 24h (sanity checks, smoke), then 5% for 48h (early signal), then 20% ramp to full if stable.
- Rollback triggers (automated):
  - Any single prompt with harm > 5x baseline in the canary -> immediate rollback.
  - Aggregate safety_harm_rate increase > 0.2 absolute -> rollback.
  - Helpfulness delta < -1.0% at 20% traffic and still negative at 48h -> pause.

I'll own the eval dashboards and can ship the initial sampling harness today; need Karthik to tag prompt IDs in telemetry.

Marissa
Lead, Evaluation Systems
